# Monaco readiness poll throws before its registry exists

## Context

The Monaco component readiness helper introduced by PR #18355 failed an unrelated history PR's component job. [Job 101328008490](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/33973844177/job/101328008490) reports 248 passed / 1 failed: the reactive-wrapper case throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'monaco-test-editor')` in `expectEditor`, before polling can wait. A later attempt is green; the premature lookup remains reproducible.

## The Problem

`test/playwright/component/wrapper/MonacoEditor.spec.mjs#expectEditor` evaluates `addon?.map[id]`. The addon namespace can exist before its editor registry does. Optional chaining guards the addon, while the missing registry is still indexed.

Executing the exact callback with an absent addon returns false; with `addon = {}` it throws TypeError; with an empty registry it returns false; with a ready editor/model it returns true. A real `getModel` exception propagates.

## The Architectural Reality

This is a test-observation race. The helper already owns the not-ready predicate and the bounded `expect.poll`; the addon, wrapper and history implementation need no behavioral change. Its existing JSDoc requires an actual native editor rather than an empty wrapper div.

## The Fix

Guard the registry access within the existing predicate. Preserve the readiness/model checks and the existing poll bound. Do not catch arbitrary browser exceptions or increase retries/timeouts.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| expectEditor callback | existing helper/JSDoc | false until registry/editor/model exist and addon is ready | genuine model errors still propagate | existing helper summary | direct callback state controls; existing six real component cases |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Absent addon, namespace-before-registry and empty registry all produce false without throwing; a ready editor/model produces true.
- [ ] A genuine exception from an existing editor's `getModel` still propagates.
- [ ] The existing six Monaco component cases pass through the named component configuration.

## Out of Scope

Monaco runtime APIs, DOMPurify remediation, history semantics, new retries/timeouts and broader test-harness changes.

## Avoided Traps

A blanket catch would hide a real editor failure. Re-running CI alone does not repair the callback's invalid intermediate-state assumption.
